summary: Scythe is a slow-building area-control engine game where five asymmetric factions expand across a hex map, gathering resources and building up mechs and territory while mostly avoiding direct combat until it's decisive. The gorgeous production and quiet tension of watching engines grow make it feel more like a Euro with a war painted on top than an actual wargame.
praised: asymmetric factions and player mats create varied strategies
combat is rare but meaningful, avoiding constant conflict
criticised: combat can feel anticlimactic or swingy when it happens
long setup and playtime for its actual depth
some factions/mats are stronger than others
can feel like a multiplayer solitaire race to end triggers

interaction.detail: Factions move units and mechs across one shared hex map, contesting territory and triggering combat that can eliminate opponents' pieces or steal resources. Encounter cards and popularity tracks add further ways one player's choices constrain or hurt another.

scoring.how_you_win: Be the first to complete your sixth star through combat, building, popularity or objectives, ending the game; then total coins plus popularity-multiplied resources, territories, buildings and recruits — highest score wins.
scoring.score_note: popularity multiplier can push it higher

similar: Rise of Fenris (Scythe's own campaign expansion)
